brief:
The International Criminal Court's arrest warrant against Benjamin Netanyahu would remain in force even if he stepped down as Israeli prime minister, according to Middle East Eye. Leaving office would eliminate one legal shield his supporters cite — immunity granted to sitting heads of state — but neither the warrant itself nor the underlying genocide case would be dismissed by a change in his governmental status.

ICC arrest warrants operate independently of a suspect's official position. The court's legal framework does not provide immunity to former leaders, meaning Netanyahu could potentially face arrest in signatory countries regardless of when he exits office.

title: Netanyahu's ICC warrant persists regardless of his tenure
